meta.title: Football, Visualized — interactive xG playground
meta.description: Move the shooter, goalkeeper and defenders, explore eight positional inputs, and inspect an independent xG model’s methodology. A project by Leonardo Ferreira.

playground.title: Build the chance.
playground.description: Move the players. See how positions change the inputs and the estimate.
playground.status: Independent model trained on StatsBomb Open Data. This positional scene is illustrative, has partial visibility and does not give a specific player’s exact probability.
playground.pitchDescription: Attacking half of the pitch with movable strikers, center-backs and a goalkeeper. Drag a player or focus one and use the arrow keys.
playground.keyboardHint: Use the arrow keys to move this player. Hold Shift for larger steps.

methodology.title: Behind the estimate
methodology.intro: A playground for understanding goal-scoring chances and inspecting how data, modeling choices and engineering reach the number on screen.
methodology.overview: An estimate of 0.20 xG represents roughly 20 goals in 100 comparable shots according to this model. It is not an exact probability for a particular player. Here, the invented scene simplifies real context.
methodology.data: We use StatsBomb Open Data with observed goal/non-goal outcomes; source xG is never the target. The population consists of male open-play foot shots. Headers, penalties and other situations are excluded from training. Event frames are the primary observation; optional 360 availability does not guarantee all defenders are visible. Missing keepers and singular goal-line cases are excluded, without imputation.
methodology.featuresIntro: Geometry describes the opportunity; counts and distances describe observed opponents. The cone is the finite triangle between shot and posts. Positions use meters independently of SVG. With zero defenders, distance uses the pitch diagonal sentinel alongside the explicit count. Other attackers, identity, preferred foot, technique, speed and temporal context are omitted.
methodology.training: Whole matches are separated into training, calibration, selection and test, avoiding shared match events between groups. Bounded search uses five folds on training only; logistic scaling is fitted within each fold. Three logistic regressions isolate geometry, defenders and all inputs. Shallow XGBoost tests nonlinear interactions. There is no class balancing or post-selection refit.
methodology.selection: The declared rule selected XGBoost using observed performance and the Brier deterioration guardrail for preferring simplicity. Selection intervals did not establish conclusive superiority. Sigmoid calibration did not meet adoption criteria. Freezing means fixing inputs, preprocessing, trees and calibration before opening the final test; the interface only executes those parameters.
methodology.scores: Log loss penalizes confident wrong probabilities; Brier measures squared probability error. Lower is better. Selection chooses the model; final test evaluates the already fixed model. It was not used for retuning. The 95% intervals resample whole matches, preserving shot dependence.
methodology.final: Final test held out until freezing
methodology.paired: XGBoost minus reference: negative values favor XGBoost. Overall intervals favor the candidate on this test; this does not guarantee an advantage in every slice or transfer to other competitions or scenes.
methodology.calibration: The diagonal represents agreement between predicted mean and observed frequency. Bars show match-based 95% intervals of observed frequency; hollow points mark sparse bins. No supported bin was flagged, but high-probability ranges have few examples and do not support precision for extreme scenes.
methodology.slices: With two defenders inside the cone, XGBoost was worse than full logistic on this test. This refers to the cone count, not the total on the pitch. We keep this result visible; overall averages do not erase local failures.
methodology.support: The descriptive reference uses neighbors in standardized training-only features, with a 99% threshold and a separate zero-defender cohort. We do not publish reference rows, so the interface does not calculate joint support for each edit. Four open-play presets fall outside this reference; being inside does not prove realism either. Rare scenes remain explorable. Comparisons are not causal effects; partial visibility, few defenders and other domains limit interpretation.
methodology.inference: TypeScript extracts the same eight inputs as the Python pipeline. The loader validates and captures immutable parameters; XGBoost preserves float32 comparisons/accumulation within 1e-7 tolerance. Trees may retain the result after small movements. Invalid inputs or unavailable models receive no substitute heuristic. Penalties use the fixed 0.76 convention, separate from the learned model.
methodology.review: Scientific review was accepted with limitations and distribution of the exact artifact was reviewed for the free/non-commercial scope. The original automatic status remains “needs_review”; review does not authorize publication. Private training and complete reproduction were run by the owner; the assistant reviewed aggregates/checks without rerunning private data.
